method: Official patriarchal, diocesan, parish, and Luxembourg church-recognition sources were checked. Current official bodies are preserved in parallel even when they fall outside the four communities named in the state convention.

candidates.name: Saints Anargyres Orthodox Parish in Luxembourg
candidates.reason: Official historical and Luxembourg recognition pages describe the Saints Anargyres chapel at 3 Rue Pulvermuhl. The current Metropolis parish list instead names Saint Volodymyr Equal-to-the-Apostles as its second Luxembourg parish, and the former Saints Anargyres page now carries Saint Volodymyr's Dommeldange details. The cathedral and Saint Volodymyr parish are published; a third row waits for current confirmation that Saints Anargyres still exists as a separate body.

historical_or_superseded.name: Russian Orthodox house church in Wiltz
historical_or_superseded.status: historical predecessor, not a separate current body
historical_or_superseded.reason: The official ROCOR history records the house church founded in Wiltz in 1927 as the beginning of the community that later built Saints Peter and Paul Church in Luxembourg. The current 2026 diocesan directory lists only Saints Peter and Paul in Luxembourg and no separate Wiltz body.
